title: Geometric cohomology criterion and internal-Hom finiteness for native Weil complexes
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, and $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Let $X_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and let $g$ be geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. On $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ put $R_X=p_X^*\underline\Omega$ for the finite-subextension-valued coefficient ring [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and $\mathcal A_X=\operatorname{Mod}(R_X)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $\mathcal B_X=\mathcal A_X^{g^*}$ for sheaves with invertible Frobenius structure [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]. Let $U:D(\mathcal B_X)\to D(\mathcal A_X)$ be termwise forgetting Frobenius in the ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, lem-sf-weil-native-closed-forgetful]. Let $\mathrm{WC}(X_0)\subset D(\mathcal B_X)$ be the full subcategory whose cohomology vanishes outside a finite interval and whose underlying cohomology modules admit a finite locally closed constructible stratification with pro-etale locally finite free restrictions, using the native module presentation of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework] and its comparison [lem-sf-weil-verdier-module-constructibility-comparison]. Let $\Dbc(X,\Omega)$ and $\Dctf(X,\Omega)$ have the finite-scalar-local-model and finite-Tor-amplitude meanings of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], and use the ambient relative derived sheaf internal Hom of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom].

For every $M\in D(\mathcal B_X)$, one has $M\in\mathrm{WC}(X_0)$ if and only if $UM\in\Dbc(X,\Omega)$. This criterion preserves and reflects each finite cohomological support interval. For every $K,L\in\mathrm{WC}(X_0)$, both $UK$ and $UL$ belong to $\Dctf(X,\Omega)$ and
$$R\mathcal Hom_{R_X}(UK,UL)\in\Dctf(X,\Omega)\subset\Dbc(X,\Omega).$$
The latter conclusion includes bounded cohomology and constructibility for arbitrary such $K,L$; no lissity or site-perfectness of $K$ is imposed. It concerns geometric relative sheaf Hom and makes no assertion about Frobenius-invariant global Hom groups.

proof.text: Apply separated finite-type base change to $X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ along $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$. Thus $X$ is separated of finite type over the field $k$, so it is a standing scheme for the geometric constructibility results below. The algebraic extension $k/k_0$ has the same positive characteristic, different from $\ell$.

Let U be the abelian forgetful functor from invertible Frobenius structures and let F be native scalar-forgetting followed by transport along nativeModuleCoefficientIso. The native module comparison supplies an equivalence whose functor is F followed by the existing sectionwise presentation. Its faithfulness and that of the presentation make F faithful; U is faithful as well. Exactness of U and F and the exact-functor homology comparison identify H^n of the displayed composite derived functor with F(U(H^n M)). The sectionwise equivalence unit and the constructibility clause of the native comparison identify native constructible sheaves with finite constant scalar models. Isomorphism invariance follows through the adic constructibility predicate comparison. Apply this degreewise and use preservation and reflection of boundedness by faithful exact functors to prove the Weil-complex criterion. For each prescribed interval, apply the same homology isomorphism: forward vanishing follows by preservation of zero, and reverse vanishing by faithfulness applied to the identity morphism. This works also for reversed or empty support intervals.

proof.text: For $K,L\in\mathrm{WC}(X_0)$, step 2 gives $UK,UL\in\Dbc(X,\Omega)$. The field-coefficient equality $\Dctf=\Dbc$ in the constructible-heart statement applies with $\Lambda=\Omega=\Qlb$. Hence $UK,UL\in\Dctf(X,\Omega)$; this is finite Tor amplitude of the complexes, not a claim of site-perfectness.

For $K,L\in\mathrm{WC}(X_0)$, step 2 gives $UK,UL\in\Dbc(X,\Omega)$. A field is Noetherian, so by step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] the scheme $X$ is Noetherian. Hence [lem-sfb-adic-constructibility-predicate-comparison], for the finite-subextension-valued ring $\Omega$ of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], identifies $\Dbc(X,\Omega)$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible] with the bounded constructible subcategory of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], as object properties of the same derived category. So $UK,UL$ are bounded constructible in the latter sense. The coefficient $\underline{\Qlb}$ case of [lem-sfb-dc-hom-small-coefficients] is this same finite-subextension ring, and step 1 supplies its scheme hypothesis. It shows that the ambient relative internal Hom $R\mathcal Hom_{R_X}(UK,UL)$ of [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] is bounded constructible. The same comparison returns it to $\Dbc(X,\Omega)$. The field equality $\Dctf=\Dbc$ of [sk-lem-coefficient-heart] for $\Lambda=\Qlb$ places it in $\Dctf(X,\Omega)$, a full subcategory of $\Dbc(X,\Omega)$ by definition. Both arguments are arbitrary; no lissity or site-perfectness of $K$ is used. The admissible-coefficient internal-Hom stability theorem is not applied: its $\Qlb$ is the full continuous-map ring $C(-,\Qlb)$ of the localizing-closure convention, a different condensed ring.
